name: Video Color Balance
description: Monitors white balance and color temperature stability across the video timeline, detecting abrupt chromatic shifts that betray frame-level independent color processing in AI-generated sequences.
algorithm: Video Color Balance — Pixel-Level Spatial Analysis
mechanism:
This method analyzes video color balance for forensic detection:

1. **White Balance Estimation**: The illuminant color temperature is estimated per frame using white point detection, gray world assumption, and highlight analysis. The estimated white balance should be consistent across the frame and stable over time.

2. **Face-Background White Balance Comparison**: The effective white balance of the face and background should match (same illumination). The method compares white point estimates from face and background. Deepfake face insertion may introduce a face rendered under different white balance — warmer or cooler color temperature than the environment.

3. **Color Channel Balance**: The RGB channel balance (relative mean values) is tracked across frames. Natural video shows stable channel balance within scenes. Deepfake generation may produce subtle channel imbalances, particularly visible in neutral-colored face regions where white balance errors become apparent.

4. **Color Cast Detection**: The method detects unwanted color casts (systematic color shift) in the face compared to the surrounding area. Even sophisticated deepfakes may impart subtle color casts from the training data or generator's learned bias, producing faces with slightly different color bias than the scene.

5. **Temporal Color Balance Stability**: Color balance should vary slowly with lighting changes. The method tracks color balance stability — high-frequency color balance fluctuations in the face region (while background remains stable) indicate per-frame independent color rendering in the deepfake generation process.
parameters:
Analysis type: pixel
Media: video
Input: Video frames extracted at key intervals
Output: Confidence score (0-100)
Frame sampling: Adaptive (1-5 fps depending on method)
Temporal window: Sliding window across frame sequence
accuracy: Moderate to High — 70-88% standalone accuracy. Most effective when combined with other video forensic methods. Performance depends on video quality, resolution, and compression level.
source: Video forensics and deepfake detection research. Based on computer vision and temporal signal analysis methods.
useCase: Detection of deepfake and AI-generated video through video color balance analysis. This method examines temporal and spatial features that are difficult for AI systems to perfectly replicate, providing evidence for video authenticity assessment.
strengths:
• Captures temporal artifacts that single-frame analysis misses
• Works with standard video formats
• Effective against common deepfake techniques
• Can be combined with other video forensic methods
• Based on established computer vision research
limitations:
• Performance affected by video compression and resolution
• Some methods require sufficient frame count for temporal analysis
• Effectiveness varies with deepfake generation technique
• Best used as part of a comprehensive multi-method pipeline
• May produce false positives on heavily edited authentic video

references.title: Verdoliva, L. (2020). Media Forensics and DeepFakes: An Overview. IEEE JSTSP.
Zheng, Y. et al. (2021). Exploring Temporal Coherence for More General Video Face Forgery Detection. ICCV.
